Infinite graphs may correspond to multiple indices so we will take that the corresponding subfactor planar algebras has index 4 as a given.

Lemma 12.1
.

The trace of any minimal projection in
\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{P}}
is 1.

Proof.

First we prove by induction that for all
k\geq 0
,
\text{tr}(P_{k})+\text{tr}(Q_{k})=2
, where we define
P_{0}=Q_{0}=\emptyset_{+}
. The base cases follow from
\text{tr}(\emptyset_{+})=1
and from the index being 4 since,
\text{tr}(X)=2=\text{tr}(P_{1})+\text{tr}(Q_{1})
. Assume the claim is true up to some
k\in\mathbb{N}
. The principal graph gives that
2\text{tr}(P_{k})=\text{tr}(P_{k-1})+\text{tr}(P_{k+1})
and
2\text{tr}(Q_{k})=\text{tr}(Q_{k-1})+\text{tr}(Q_{k+1})
. Adding these two equations together and using the inductive hypothesis gives
\text{tr}(P_{k+1})+\text{tr}(Q_{k+1})=2
. Therefore, for all
k\geq 0
,
\text{tr}(P_{k})+\text{tr}(Q_{k})=2
. The same process shows the analogous result for the dual principal graph.

Now suppose that
\text{tr}(P_{1})\neq 1
, which also implies
\text{tr}(Q_{1})\neq 1
. Either
P_{1}
or
Q_{1}
will have trace less than one by the preceding paragraph, so without loss of generality assume
\text{tr}(P_{1})<1
. We then show that
(\text{tr}(P_{k}))_{k\in\mathbb{N}}
is a strictly decreasing sequence. By the principal graph,
\text{tr}(P_{1})=\frac{1+\text{tr}(P_{2})}{2}
. That is,
\text{tr}(P_{1})
is the arithmetic mean of 1 and
\text{tr}(P_{2})
. Since
\text{tr}(P_{1})<1
, this means
\text{tr}(P_{2})<\text{tr}(P_{1})
, as desired. Assume up to some
k
,
\text{tr}(P_{k+1})<\text{tr}(P_{k})
. The trace of
P_{k+1}
is the arithmetic mean of the trace of
P_{k}
and the trace of
P_{k+2}
, so its value lies in between the two values. Since
\text{tr}(P_{k+1})<\text{tr}(P_{k})
, this gives that
\text{tr}(P_{k+2})<\text{tr}(P_{k+1})
. Thus
(\text{tr}(P_{k}))_{k\in\mathbb{N}}
is a strictly decreasing sequence. As the graph is infinite, this means there is some
N\in\mathbb{N}
where
\text{tr}(P_{N})<0
. However, since the inner product is positive definite and
P_{N}
is a minimal projection, we reach a contradiction. Therefore,
\text{tr}(P_{1})=1
and
\text{tr}(Q_{1})=1
. By shifting the starting term of the infinite sequence in the above argument,
\text{tr}(P_{k})=\text{tr}(Q_{k})=1
. The same argument applies for the dual principal graph. Thus the trace of all minimal projections is 1. ∎

Next, we can follow the same process as done for the
\tilde{A}_{2n-1}
subfactor planar algebras. As we can just ignore any lemma or part of a proof involving isomorphism
P_{n}\cong Q_{n}
, these proofs are easier adaptations of the finite affine
A
case and will thus be omitted. We then get the following theorems.

Theorem 12.2
.

(Necessary relations for
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
)
If
\mathcal{P}
is a subfactor planar algebra with principal and dual principal graph the
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
subfactor planar algebra then
\mathcal{P}
has diagrammatic elements
P_{1}
and
Q_{1}
from Definition
3.1
with relations (i) through (iv) of Definition
3.2
. Further, we get the equivalence classes of minimal projections are:

Theorem 12.3
.

(Sufficient relations for
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
)
Let
\mathcal{P}
be the planar algebra with generator
P_{1}
from Definition
3.1
with relations (i) through (iv) given in Definition
3.2
. Define
P_{1}
and
Q_{1}
to be self-adjoint, then extend the * operation anti-linearly and on diagrams. Then
\mathcal{P}
is a subfactor planar algebra whose principal graph an dual principal graph are the
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
ones given in Theorem
12.2
.

Theorem 12.4
.

The elements
P_{1}
and
Q_{1}
from Theorem
12.2
generate the planar algebra
\mathcal{P}
in that theorem.

The following theorem, which is a known result by Popa
[
Pop94
]
, is then direct from the planar algebra presentation.

Theorem 12.5
.

There is exactly one subfactor planar algebra with principal graph
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
up to isomorphism.

We now mimic the unshaded
\tilde{A}_{2n-1}
planar algebra section for unshaded
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
planar algebras. From now on, let
\mathcal{P}
be an unshaded subfactor planar algebra with principal graph the
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
Dynkin diagram. Define

Theorem 12.7
.

(Sufficient relations for
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
, unshaded: Arrow case)
Let
\mathcal{P}
be the planar algebra generated by
P_{1}
from Definition
6.1
with relations from Definition
6.2
. Define
P_{1}
to be self-adjoint and extend * anti-linearly and on diagrams. The
\mathcal{P}
is an unshaded subfactor planar algebra who principal graph is given in the arrow case of Theorem
12.6
.

Theorem 12.8
.

The element
P_{1}
from Definition
6.1
generates the planar algebra
\mathcal{P}
from Theorem
12.6
in the arrow case.

Theorem 12.9
.

(Sufficient relations for
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
, unshaded: Color Case)
Let
\mathcal{P}
be the planar algebra generated by
P_{1}
and
Q_{1}
from Definition
6.3
with relations (i) through (iv) from Definition
6.4
. Define
P_{1}
and
Q_{1}
to be self-adjoint and extend * anti-linearly and on diagrams. Then
\mathcal{P}
is an unshaded subfactor planar algebra whose principal graph is given in the color case of Theorem
12.6
.

Theorem 12.10
.

The elements
P_{1}
and
Q_{1}
from Definition
6.3
generate the subfactor planar algebra
\mathcal{P}
in the color case of Theorem
12.6
.

Theorem 12.11
.

There are exactly two nonisomorphic unshaded subfactor planar algebras with principal graph
\tilde{A}_{\infty}
.

Remark 12.1
.

By Popa’s
[
Pop94
]
classification, there are additionally type
\tilde{D}
and type
\tilde{E}
index 4 subfactor planar algebras. Work forthcoming by the author will display similar presentations of these subfactor planar algebras. In particular, this will complete the Kuperberg program for index 4 subfactors.
